::: {#exm-rao-blackwell-poisson}
#### Rao--Blackwellizing an estimate of the chance of a zero count

The `birthwt` data record the number of previous premature labors (`ptl`) for `r nrow(read.csv("data/birthwt.csv"))` women
in a study at Baystate Medical Center in Springfield, Massachusetts
[@hosmer1989applied]; the data ship with the R package
[`MASS`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=MASS) (`MASS::birthwt`),
and this site has a copy at [`data/birthwt.csv`](data/birthwt.csv).
Treat counts like these as a Poisson sample, $\dsn{X} \siid \Pois(\rate)$,
with $\rate$ equal to the mean of `ptl`, `r round(mean(read.csv("data/birthwt.csv")$ptl), 3)`.

The estimand is the probability of a zero count,
$\prob = \Pr(\Rvar_\iobs = 0) = e^{-\rate}$.
Index the model by $\prob$ instead of $\rate$ (the map $\rate \mapsto e^{-\rate}$ is one-to-one);
then the sum $S = \sumin \Rvar_\iobs$ is still [sufficient](#def-sufficient), by @exm-poisson-sufficient.

The crude estimator is the indicator that the first observation is zero,
$\hprob_1 = \indiccb{X_1 = 0}$, which uses one observation and is unbiased for $\prob$.
Its Rao--Blackwellization is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\hprob_2
&= \condE{\hprob_1}{S}
&& \text{(definition of the Rao--Blackwellized estimator)}\\
&= \Pr\paren{X_1 = 0 \given S}
&& \text{(the mean of an indicator is a probability)}\\
&= \paren{\frac{n-1}{n}}^S
&& \text{(conditional probability of a zero)}
\end{aligned}
$$

By @lem-poisson-zero-rb, the conditional probability in the last line is the one in @eq-poisson-zero-conditional.
For $n = 20$ we draw 10,000 samples, compute both estimators on each,
and report each one's mean (with a 95% confidence interval)
and variance (with a 95% confidence interval from the normal approximation
to the sampling distribution of a sample variance).

```{r}
#| label: rao-blackwell-poisson-sim
#| code-fold: true
birthwt <- read.csv("data/birthwt.csv")

# The Poisson rate: the observed mean number of previous premature labors.
lambda <- mean(birthwt$ptl)
# The estimand: the probability of a zero count.
pi_true <- exp(-lambda)

n <- 20
n_reps <- 10000

set.seed(1945)
# One row per sample of n counts.
samples <- matrix(rpois(n * n_reps, lambda), nrow = n_reps)
s_sum <- rowSums(samples)

# The crude estimator and its Rao-Blackwellization.
est <- data.frame(
  crude = as.numeric(samples[, 1] == 0),
  rao_blackwell = ((n - 1) / n)^s_sum
)

# Mean with a t interval; variance with a normal-approximation interval,
# using the standard error sqrt((m4 - s^4) / N) of a sample variance.
summarize_estimator <- function(x) {
  tt <- t.test(x)
  v <- var(x)
  m4 <- mean((x - mean(x))^4)
  se_v <- sqrt((m4 - v^2) / length(x))
  data.frame(
    mean = mean(x),
    mean_lower = tt$conf.int[1],
    mean_upper = tt$conf.int[2],
    variance = v,
    var_lower = v - 1.96 * se_v,
    var_upper = v + 1.96 * se_v
  )
}
rb_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(est, summarize_estimator))
round(rb_summary, 4)
```

```{r}
#| label: rao-blackwell-poisson-ratio
#| include: false
var_ratio <- rb_summary["crude", "variance"] /
  rb_summary["rao_blackwell", "variance"]
```

The estimand is $\prob =$ `r round(pi_true, 3)`.
Both estimators have simulated means near it, as @thm-rb-unbiased says they must.
The variance of the Rao--Blackwellized estimator is about `r round(var_ratio, 1)` times smaller than that of the crude estimator,
as @thm-rao-blackwell requires.

```{r}
#| label: fig-rao-blackwell-poisson-alt
#| include: false
fig_alt_rb <- sprintf(
  paste(
    "Two histograms of the simulated estimates, one panel for each estimator,",
    "with a vertical line at the estimand %.3f.",
    "The crude estimator takes only the values 0 and 1;",
    "the Rao-Blackwellized estimator takes many values between",
    "%.2f and %.2f, clustered around the estimand."
  ),
  pi_true, min(est$rao_blackwell), max(est$rao_blackwell)
)
```

::: {#fig-rao-blackwell-poisson}

```{r}
#| label: rao-blackwell-poisson-plot
#| fig-alt: !expr fig_alt_rb
#| code-fold: true
est_long <- data.frame(
  estimate = c(est$crude, est$rao_blackwell),
  estimator = rep(
    c("crude (first observation is zero)", "Rao-Blackwellized"),
    each = n_reps
  )
)
p <- ggplot(est_long, aes(x = estimate)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = pi_true, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~estimator, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "estimate of the probability of a zero count", y = "count")
if (knitr::is_html_output()) plotly::ggplotly(p) else p
```

The sampling distribution of the crude and Rao--Blackwellized estimators ($n = 20$, 10,000 samples); the dashed line marks the estimand
